newsitem.title: SENEGAL: Senegal's phosphate workers on strike.
newsitem.headline: Senegal's phosphate workers on strike.

text.p: Workers at Senegal's Societe Senegalaise des Phosphates de Thies (SSPT) went on strike for a 25 percent pay rise on Wednesday, a workers' union leader said.
"As far as they don't satisfy our demand we will not go back to work," SSPT organiser Fally Badji told Reuters by telephone from Lam Lam, 70 km from the capital Dakar.
Management at the 50 percent state-owned firm, which employs 154 people and is earmarked for privatisation, were offering only 2.8 percent, said a SSPT workers' union official.
"We cannot offer more than 2.8 percent of pay rise to all of our workers," said a company spokesman.
SSPT produced 64,000 tonnes of phosphate in 1996.
Phosphate is used commercially in a wide range of products, including crop fertilizers.
